sections.title: Biotech Research and Drug Discovery Agents
sections.description: For Biogen (Cambridge HQ), Vertex Pharmaceuticals (Boston HQ), and Boston's world-class biotech research community.

blocks.heading: Scientific literature surveillance agents
paragraphs: Autonomous agents continuously monitoring PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv, and conference proceedings for publications relevant to Biogen's therapeutic areas (multiple sclerosis, neurodegeneration, rare diseases) — synthesizing new findings into structured weekly briefings for research scientists and surfacing publications that potentially impact Biogen's pipeline programs.

blocks.heading: Competitor pipeline intelligence agents
paragraphs: Autonomous agents monitoring the FDA's clinical trial database (ClinicalTrials.gov), SEC filings, conference presentations, and press releases for Biogen's and Vertex's competitors' drug development activities — maintaining a continuously updated competitive intelligence picture for strategic planning.

blocks.heading: Patent landscape monitoring agents
paragraphs: Autonomous agents tracking patent applications and grants in Biogen's and Vertex's therapeutic areas — alerting IP counsel when new patents appear that may affect freedom-to-operate for pipeline compounds.
Self-hosted on corporate infrastructure — research IP and competitive intelligence stays within the company network.

sections.title: Clinical Trial Management Agents
sections.description: For the CROs (IQVIA, Covance/Labcorp, PRA Health Sciences) and pharma companies running trials from Boston.

blocks.heading: Clinical trial enrollment monitoring agents
paragraphs: Autonomous agents monitoring enrollment progress across trial sites, identifying sites falling behind enrollment targets, and generating corrective action recommendations for clinical operations teams managing multi-site Phase II and III trials.

blocks.heading: Protocol deviation detection agents
paragraphs: Agents continuously reviewing incoming clinical data for protocol deviations, Good Clinical Practice (GCP) compliance issues, and data quality alerts — dramatically reducing the time between deviation occurrence and detection for the clinical quality teams managing trials under FDA oversight.

blocks.heading: Regulatory submission preparation agents
paragraphs: Autonomous agents aggregating and formatting the clinical trial data packages required for FDA IND updates, NDA submissions, and safety reporting — reducing the manual data compilation that consumes significant clinical regulatory affairs effort.

sections.title: Investment Research Intelligence Agents
sections.description: For Fidelity Investments (Boston HQ), Wellington Management, and Boston's large investment management community.

blocks.heading: Biotech pipeline intelligence agents for biotech-focused funds
paragraphs: Autonomous agents monitoring the FDA's approval calendar, clinical trial outcomes, and biotech company pipeline progress for the biotech-focused investment funds that are disproportionately represented in Boston's investment management community.

blocks.heading: Corporate event monitoring agents
paragraphs: Autonomous agents tracking earnings releases, guidance updates, management changes, and SEC filings for the companies in Fidelity's large research coverage universe — generating structured event summaries for research analysts.

blocks.heading: Fixed income credit event agents
paragraphs: Autonomous agents monitoring credit events, covenant compliance, and debt maturity schedules for Wellington's large fixed income investment programs.

sections.title: FDA Regulatory Intelligence Agents
sections.description: For Boston's large biotech and MedTech regulatory affairs community.

blocks.heading: FDA regulatory action monitoring agents
paragraphs: Autonomous agents tracking FDA Warning Letters, 483 observations, advisory committee meeting outcomes, and regulatory guidance document updates relevant to Boston biotech companies' regulatory strategies.

blocks.heading: 510(k) and PMA clearance intelligence
paragraphs: Autonomous agents monitoring FDA's device clearance database for the Boston MedTech companies tracking competitor device clearances and the regulatory precedents they set for similar device applications.

sections.title: Boston AI agent standards
sections.description: Key compliance standards for Boston AI agent deployments.

blocks.heading: Scientific accuracy is non-negotiable
paragraphs: Boston's biotech and academic communities will not tolerate autonomous agents that hallucinate scientific facts or misattribute research findings. ClickMasters designs Boston research agents with mandatory source citation, confidence scoring, and explicit uncertainty signaling — agents that say 'I don't have sufficient evidence to confirm this' rather than generating plausible-sounding but unverified scientific claims.

blocks.heading: Self-hosted for all biotech research agents
paragraphs: Biogen's competitive intelligence, Vertex's pipeline status, and Boston's biotech research IP cannot be processed by external API-based agents. All Boston biotech agents are deployed on client corporate infrastructure.

blocks.heading: GCP and 21 CFR Part 11 for clinical agents
paragraphs: Clinical trial agents producing records that may be submitted to the FDA must comply with 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements and Good Clinical Practice guidelines — ClickMasters builds clinical agents with this regulatory framework as baseline.
